summary: MVP discipline is strong: 7/9 stages are script-only at L1, ~$0 per 50-CR batch, and only three stages ever admit LLM (Runbook/Rollback L3 ceilings, Risk Synthesis L2 SOTA). Three blockers undermine P0 gates as written: SLA impact arithmetic double-counts overlapping maintenance, the <$2 batch budget is incompatible with Risk Synthesis L2 at target scale, and synthetic eval is structurally tautological for L1 (explicit service names + definitional injections) while USE-CASE claims agent irreplaceability. Five concerns cover synthetic realism for overnight-agent eval, weak LLM justification for Runbook L3 and CAB narrative, P0 metric overclaiming (Prior Auth #3 parallel), Schedule+SLA merge blind spots, and untrusted optional PR scope flags.

l1_mvp.notes: All script/template; wall-clock <5 min per doc

l2_target_sota_no_l3.breakdown: Runbook+Rollback encoder ~$0.50; Historical embedding ~$0.15; Risk L2 LLM ~$1.00–$4.00 ($0.02–$0.08/CR × 50)
l2_target_sota_no_l3.notes: Upper bound exceeds stated <$2 batch gate if Risk L2 runs on every CR

l3_worst_case_high_risk_subset.notes: Budget rule caps one of Runbook/Rollback L3 per CR unless tier-1+high; still conflicts with full-batch Risk L2

findings.title: SLA arithmetic sums full durations — double-counts overlapping windows
findings.observation: Stage 6 sums `expected_duration_min` per service tier and compares to remaining monthly budget. Scheduling conflict detection uses interval overlap on shared services, but SLA math does not use overlap geometry or concurrent maintenance modeling.
findings.challenge: If CR-A and CR-B overlap 60 minutes on `payment-service`, wall-clock customer impact is ~60 minutes, not 120. Summing both durations will false-flag SLA breach (#4) and corrupt aggregate SLA dashboard in Stage 9.
findings.recommendation: Define SLA downtime as interval-union per (service, tier) across the CAB window: merge overlapping [start,end] intervals, sum merged lengths, then compare to budget. Keep scheduling-pair recall on pairwise overlap; decouple SLA metric to union-based arithmetic. Add injected GT cases where overlap exists but sum-of-durations would breach while union would not.
findings.evidence: Schedule & SLA L1: 'sum expected_duration_min per service tier'; overlap detection is separate 'interval overlap on shared affected_services'

findings.title: Pipeline budget gate contradicts Risk Synthesis L2 SOTA at 50-CR scale
findings.observation: USE-CASE and Pipeline Budget Gate require <$2 per 50-CR batch. Risk Synthesis L2 is SOTA at ~$0.02–$0.08/CR (~$1–$4 per batch). L2 encoder costs add ~$0.10–$0.30. Architecture states Risk L2 runs as last stage with bounded output tokens but does not cap CR count or make L2 optional at P0.
findings.challenge: Target architecture cannot simultaneously be 'SOTA = L2 narrative on every CR' and '<$2 for 50 CRs' without selective routing. Teams will either blow budget or silently stay on L1 while claiming SOTA.
findings.recommendation: Split budgets: P0 MVP gate = L1-only <$0.05; Target gate = Risk L2 on flagged CRs only (conditional/reject path, or tier-1/high-risk) with measured token cap. Document expected % of CRs receiving L2. Alternatively raise batch budget to $5 with explicit per-CR ceiling.
findings.evidence: Pipeline Budget Gate: '< $2 for a 50-CR CAB window'; Risk Synthesis L2: '~$0.02-0.08/CR'; E2E metric #6 cost < $2

findings.title: P0 synthetic+L1 eval is tautological for core agent claims
findings.observation: Generator injects failures with explicit CMDB service names in runbooks (L1 string match). Historical Pattern L1 exact tuple match hits injected #7 by construction. CAB recommendation GT is derived from the same deterministic rollup rules implemented in Stage 9. Architecture admits synthetic is an upper bound but P0 gates (≥80% recall, ≥75% CAB accuracy) do not require noise/messiness tiers before pass.
findings.challenge: Passing P0 does not falsify the USE-CASE claim that cross-artifact semantic reasoning is agent-irreplaceable — it mostly proves the injection script and rule engine mirror each other. Overnight-agent eval value is unproven until messiness knobs are gated.
findings.recommendation: Add mandatory P0 sub-gates: (1) recall on medium+ noise injection ≥70% before build complete; (2) report per-dimension recall on prose-embedded failure subset only; (3) rename 'CAB recommendation accuracy' to 'rollup rule self-consistency' until P2. Block commercial/STRONGEST narrative on synthetic-only pass.
findings.evidence: Runbook L1 starting level: 'ITIL-template runbooks... name services explicitly'; P0 CAB accuracy vs 'deterministic severity rollup rules'; Synthetic Concentration Risk table; realism knobs 'deferred to skeptic review'

findings.title: P0 eval overclaiming parallels Prior Auth #3 (Real Data 2/5)
findings.observation: USE-CASE rates Real Data 2/5, Eval Readiness ★★★, verdict STRONGEST, Agent Score 23/25. Architecture documents P0/P2 split but E2E and USE-CASE success tables still list CAB accuracy and clean-CR FP as headline targets without synthetic-only qualifier in the metric row.
findings.challenge: Stakeholders will read ≥75% CAB accuracy and ≤15% FP as production-calibrated. Known Unknown #3 states FP and expert alignment are unmeasurable until P2 — yet no harness rubric downgrades Agent Score or blocks 'STRONGEST' labeling on synthetic pass.
findings.recommendation: Publish two scorecards in USE-CASE and ARCHITECTURE eval section: P0-Architecture (injection recall, schema, cost, wall-clock) vs P2-Production (real FP, expert alignment, actionability). Require explicit 'synthetic-only — not deployment evidence' banner on all P0 metrics in reports.
findings.evidence: USE-CASE Real Data 2/5; 'Parallels healthcare Prior Auth #3'; P0 does NOT prove list vs Success Metrics table

findings.title: Synthetic ITIL templates unlikely to stress overnight-agent cross-artifact reasoning
findings.observation: Templates are ServiceNow-shaped, ITIL-best-practice, uniform formatting. Realism knobs (prose messiness, CMDB staleness, boilerplate) are listed but not in generator acceptance criteria or P0 gates. Multi-CR windows (30+) exist but overlap/dependency failures use idealized graphs.
findings.challenge: Overnight batch processing is justified by heterogeneous reasoning burden — if L1 rules + template generator solve 90%+ without messiness, the experiment validates a rules engine batch job, not a long-running agent pattern.
findings.recommendation: Before feat build: lock generator v1 requirements — ≥5 runbook prose variants, ≥20% implicit service references, ≥15% CMDB alias drift, ≥10% optional-field omission on clean CRs. Gate P0 on recall delta between clean-template vs medium-noise subsets (trigger already in Known Unknown #1: >15% variance).
findings.evidence: Generator Design artifact templates; Realism knobs 'deferred to skeptic review'; Synthetic Concentration Risk mitigations P0 noise injection

findings.title: Runbook L3 LLM not proven necessary vs alias graph + encoder
findings.observation: L3 justified for implicit references ('payment gateway') and intent staleness ('SSH to bastion' vs VPN). L2 already does NER + semantic CMDB match. No benchmark separates entity-miss from true semantic-staleness failures.
findings.challenge: Bastion/VPN is a CMDB node `type`/`status` migration rule. Implicit gateway references are embedding + service alias table problems. L3 trigger requires L2 recall <70% AND residual errors be prose-embedded — but synthetic set won't exercise L2, so L3 may never fire or will fire on unmeasured data.
findings.recommendation: Add L2.5 Script: CMDB alias table + infrastructure-type rules (bastion, VPN endpoint, deprecated load balancer names). Require labeled holdout set of ≥50 prose-embedded stale refs before L3 approval. Demote L3 to experimental, not SOTA ceiling, until A/B shows >5% lift over L2.5.
findings.evidence: LLM Justification Runbook L3; Runbook L2 'NER... semantic similarity'; L1 note on template-clean synthetic

findings.title: Cross-dimension CAB narrative achievable with rule graph + templates
findings.observation: L2 LLM generates cross-dimension 'so what' and conditional wording. L1 already has deterministic rollup (R1–R4) and template remediation from finding types. Findings JSON includes dimension, severity, evidence, remediation per stage.
findings.challenge: Why is generation required? Example in LLM table ('staleness concerning BECAUSE rollback depends on same deprecated service') is a join on `evidence.service_ref` across dimensions — a 10-line rule, not language understanding.
findings.recommendation: Implement Risk L1.5: cross-dimension rule graph (shared service IDs, tier-1 + SLA breach + overlap triplets) emitting structured `conditional_actions[]`. Measure CAB chair actionability on same rubric; promote to L2 LLM only if L1.5 <60% actionability on ≥20 flagged CRs.
findings.evidence: Risk Synthesis L2 justification; CAB rules R1-R4; conditional triggers 'template-derived from finding type' at L1

findings.title: Merged stage misses infra-level overlap and timezone failure modes
findings.observation: Overlap only when CR pairs share exact `affected_services` entries. Normalize validates ISO-8601 but stage 6 does not document UTC normalization for overlap. No model for shared infrastructure (same K8s cluster, DB host) when service lists differ.
findings.challenge: Injected #3 will be detected on synthetic shared-service IDs; real misses happen when teams list different service names for same blast radius. Merge hides whether regression is schedule vs SLA sub-metric.
findings.recommendation: Add optional `shared_infra_tags[]` on CR normalize output for P1; P0 document limitation in eval report. Enforce UTC on window comparison. Emit sub-stage timings and separate `scheduling_conflicts` vs `sla_impact` failure codes in pipeline abort messages.
findings.evidence: Schedule overlap 'shared affected_services'; DECISIONS merge rationale; inter-stage Window calendar check

findings.title: Optional PR scope flags without provenance — rollback rules fail open
findings.observation: pr_scope_flags optional. L1 rule `schema_migration: true` + 'restore backup' → infeasible. DECISIONS accept flags from CI/CD metadata with no diff analysis. No validation that flags match change description.
findings.challenge: In production, missing or wrong flags → keyword-only rollback check misses #2 or false-negatives clean CRs. Synthetic #2 may always set flags while real CRs omit them.
findings.recommendation: P0 generator must include cases with flags absent but prose indicates migration (test keyword path). Add `scope_flags_source` and warn when flags missing on normal/emergency CRs. Inter-stage check: if description contains migration keywords and flags null, emit info finding 'scope unverified'.
findings.evidence: pr_scope_flags optional; Rollback L1 structural rules; DECISIONS PR Diff scope flags only

findings.title: LLM narrative can contradict deterministic CAB recommendation
findings.observation: L2 keeps L1 rollup for approve/conditional/reject but LLM writes narrative and conditional language. No inter-stage validator that narrative sentiment matches recommendation class.
findings.challenge: Silent degradation: JSON says approve while Markdown argues reject; CAB chair trust collapses. Cross-run consistency target drops to 85-95% at L2 but no check on recommendation↔narrative alignment.
findings.recommendation: Post-generation script gate: extract recommendation from rollup JSON; scan narrative for reject/conditional lexicon; fail or strip narrative on mismatch. Prefer L1.5 template narrative tied to rollup hash for auditability.
findings.evidence: Risk L2 'L1 severity rollup + LLM generates cross-dimension narrative'; cross-run consistency 85-95% at L2+

findings.title: Injection spec vs alert threshold mismatch; L2 trigger unreachable on synthetic
findings.observation: Failure #7 injected as ≥3 past P1 incidents; L1 alerts at ≥2 P1/P2. L2 trigger needs recall <70% on semantic category mismatch — generator uses exact categories for injections.
findings.challenge: Eval may pass with wrong severity semantics (alert on 2 vs injected 3). L2 advancement path never fires on primary dataset, creating dead evolution level for P0/P1.
findings.recommendation: Align generator and stage threshold (≥3 P1 or document why 2 is CAB-relevant). Add ≥30 injection cases with category synonym drift for L2 trigger measurement.
findings.evidence: Injection taxonomy #7; Historical Pattern L1 '≥2 past incidents'; L2 trigger recall <70% semantic mismatch

findings.title: Temporal rollback infeasibility is script-parseable before LLM L3
findings.observation: L3 example: revert Tuesday backup when change runs Thursday-Saturday. L2 extracts temporal references.
findings.challenge: This is date parsing + window comparison + backup retention policy table — deterministic. LLM L3 trigger duplicates Runbook pattern: won't fire on synthetic, expensive on edge cases.
findings.recommendation: L2.5 Script: parse backup timestamps from rollback prose, compare to `scheduled_window` from normalize.json, flag if backup age > window start − SLA RPO. Reserve L3 for <5% residual after L2.5 on held-out prose set.
findings.evidence: Rollback L3 temporal reasoning example; Rollback L2 'Extract temporal references'

findings.title: Stages 3–5 independent but forced sequential — latency headroom unused
findings.observation: Pattern Rationale admits 3–5 could fan-out; rejects due P0 scale <30 min.
findings.challenge: At 200-CR scale (Known Unknown #7), sequential multiply dominates; no evolution trigger for parallelism.
findings.recommendation: Document fan-out trigger: wall-clock >25 min at 100 CRs on L1 → parallelize 3–5 with merged checkpoint `pre-cross-cr.json`.
findings.evidence: Pattern Rationale vs fan-out; Known Unknown #7 wall-clock trigger

findings.title: CAB narrative actionability gate undefined for P0
findings.observation: L1→L2 trigger: actionability <60% human spot-check. No rater count, rubric, or sample size in Evaluation Metrics.
findings.challenge: Subjective gate cannot fire measurably during P0 build.
findings.recommendation: Add frozen 15-CR rubric (approve/conditional/reject + 'would you defer to engineer?') with 2 raters minimum; store in `.harness/evals/`.
findings.evidence: Risk L1 trigger 'human spot-check'; no corresponding Evaluation Metrics row

findings.title: Missing comms is warning — may under-represent customer-facing risk in rollup
findings.observation: Failure #6 missing comms; Completeness flags customer-facing without comms as warning. R2 needs ≥2 warnings across dimensions for conditional.
findings.challenge: Single comms warning on otherwise clean CR → approve (R3), understating regulatory/customer notification risk.
findings.recommendation: Elevate customer-facing + no comms to blocker for normal/emergency types, or auto-conditional (R2b) — align with enterprise CAB practice.
findings.evidence: Completeness L1 'no comms for customer-facing = warning'; CAB R2/R3 rules

findings.title: No direct GT — bottleneck attribution is post-hoc only
findings.observation: GT Coverage: Ingest and Normalize have no GT; evaluate via downstream failure.
findings.challenge: Parser regressions on P1 format variants look like Runbook/Completeness failures.
findings.recommendation: Golden-file tests: ≥20 ingest fixtures with expected normalize.json hash per variant.
findings.evidence: Ground Truth Coverage by Stage table Ingest/Normalize 'No GT'

per_stage_verdicts.notes: L1 script correct for defined JSON+MD bundle. Risk is parser fragility on non-generator prose (P1), not missing LLM.
Finite schema mapping. >99% field presence is measurable proxy; add golden-file hashes.
Pure ITIL predicates. Concern: comms gap severity vs CAB rollup alignment.
L1 right for baseline but synthetic will not validate L2/L3 triggers. L3 LLM not justified without L2.5 alias/rules. Encoder L2 SOTA plausible for prose refs.
L1+flags cover synthetic #2. Temporal cases need L2.5 date logic before L3 LLM. Optional flags need provenance warnings.
L1 appropriate IF SLA uses interval-union math — current sum model is wrong (blocker). Overlap detection OK for explicit shared services.
Graph algorithms correct SOTA. CMDB noise FP risk acknowledged; needs noisy-graph eval slice.
L1 tuple match tautological on synthetic. L2 embedding trigger won't fire without synonym injections. Align ≥3 vs ≥2 thresholds.
L1 correct P0 start. L2 LLM SOTA conflicts with budget; cross-dimension copy is rule-graph feasible. CAB accuracy metric circular.

debate_questions: Should P0 'done' require medium-noise generator recall within 15% of clean-template recall, or is injection-only pass sufficient for harness feat-5?
Is Risk Synthesis L2 LLM in scope for P0 at all, given <$2/50-CR gate — or should P0 ship L1 template + L1.5 rule-graph narrative only?
For SLA impact, is the correct model interval-union downtime, max-single-CR duration, or sum-of-durations (current) — and which matches enterprise SLA contracts?
Who is the trust boundary for `pr_scope_flags` in production, and should missing flags block rollback feasibility conclusions?
Should Schedule and SLA split if union-based SLA math diverges from pairwise scheduling logic, or stay merged with strictly separated sub-metrics and failure codes?
